messages.content: Change this to the past tense: Meera walks to school with her brother.
Meera walked to school with her brother.
Change I to she: I lost my keys and I looked for them everywhere.
She lost her keys and she looked for them everywhere.

Make this more formal:

Hey, can you send me the notes?
Hello, could you please send me the notes?
Make this more polite: Give me that pen.
Could you please give me that pen?

Make this shorter:

I would like to let you know that I will be arriving a little bit late to the meeting today.
I will be a little late to the meeting today.
Use simpler words for a child: The enormous elephant consumed a great quantity of foliage.
The very big elephant ate a lot of leaves.
Rewrite in the present tense: We ate rice and dal for lunch.
We eat rice and dal for lunch.

Rewrite this in the third person, about a boy called Arjun.

I wake up late and I miss the bus. I walk to school and I reach after the bell.
Arjun wakes up late and he misses the bus. He walks to school and he reaches after the bell.
Rewrite this in a casual way: I would like to inform you that I shall be late.
Just letting you know I'll be late.
Rewrite this to sound politer: Move your bag.
Could you please move your bag?

Shorten this sentence.

Due to the fact that it was raining very hard, we decided to stay at home.
Because it was raining hard, we stayed at home.

Rewrite this so a six-year-old can understand it.

Precipitation is expected throughout the afternoon.
It will rain all afternoon.

Put this sentence in the future tense.

Dad cooks dinner on Sundays.
Dad will cook dinner on Sundays.
Change "I" to "we": I like the park, and I go there on Saturdays.
We like the park, and we go there on Saturdays.

Make it formal.

I can't come tomorrow because I'm sick.
I am unable to attend tomorrow because I am unwell.

Make this request more polite.

Close the window. It's cold.
Could you please close the window? It's cold.

Rewrite this in fewer words.

The small shop at the corner of our street is where I usually go to buy my milk and bread every morning.
I buy milk and bread every morning at the small shop on our corner.

Explain this in easy words for a young child.

The feline reclined upon the cushion and observed the birds outside.
The cat lay on the cushion and watched the birds outside.
Make this past tense: The bus arrives at the corner and stops.
The bus arrived at the corner and stopped.
Rewrite this so that it is about them instead of me: I made tea and I gave it to my friends.
They made tea and they gave it to their friends.
Say this more casually: I am unable to join you for dinner this evening.
I can't join you for dinner tonight.
Please make this polite: Tell me the time.
Could you please tell me the time?
Cut this down to a shorter sentence: At this point in time, we do not have any more tickets available.
We have no tickets left.
A child needs to read this, so make it easy: We must purchase some groceries.
We have to buy some food.

Rewrite this in the present tense.

The dog barked at the gate. Then it ran into the garden. Ravi called it back.
The dog barks at the gate. Then it runs into the garden. Ravi calls it back.

Turn this into first person (I).

You told me you would come, and you brought your sister.
I told you I would come, and I brought my sister.

Please rewrite this in formal English.

Hi sir, I got your message. I'll bring the form on Monday.
Dear Sir, I have received your message. I will bring the form on Monday.
Say this more politely: Wait here.
Would you please wait here?
Make this shorter without changing the meaning: She is a person who is very good at making people laugh.
She is very good at making people laugh.
Simpler words, please, for a child: Our teacher will commence the lesson shortly.
Our teacher will start the lesson soon.
Change to the future tense: Anika is reading a book in the library.
Anika will be reading a book in the library.

Change the sentence so it is about he instead of I.

I cannot find my shoes. I think I left them at school.
He cannot find his shoes. He thinks he left them at school.
Make this sound relaxed and friendly: I am writing to confirm that I have received your parcel.
Just letting you know I got your parcel.
Rewrite so it is polite: I want some water.
May I please have some water?

Shorten this text.

Yesterday my mother and I went to the market. We walked there slowly, because it was very hot. We bought some fruit and vegetables, and then we walked back home.
My mother and I walked slowly to the market yesterday because it was hot. We bought fruit and vegetables and walked home.

Rewrite for a small child using easy words.

The infant was fatigued and fell asleep immediately.
The baby was tired and fell asleep right away.
Can you put this in the past tense? The children play cricket after school.
The children played cricket after school.
Rewrite with "she" instead of "you": You are good at drawing, and you draw every day.
She is good at drawing, and she draws every day.
Rewrite in a more formal style: We can't find the key, so please open the door.
We are unable to find the key, so please open the door.

Make this sound kinder and more polite.

You are too loud. Be quiet.
Could you please be a little quieter?
Please say this in fewer words: In the event that it rains, the match will be cancelled.
If it rains, the match is cancelled.

Use easier words for a child.

The gentleman assisted the elderly woman across the road. She expressed her gratitude.
The man helped the old woman cross the road. She said thank you.
Use the present tense instead: Grandma told us a story and we listened quietly.
Grandma tells us a story and we listen quietly.

Retell this about them (third person).

We walk to the market and we buy fruit.
They walk to the market and they buy fruit.

Turn this into casual speech.

I regret that I cannot attend the meeting. Kindly proceed without me.
Sorry, I can't make the meeting. Please go ahead without me.
Turn this into a polite request: Pass the salt.
Could you please pass the salt?
Make it briefer: My brother is taller than me, and he is also older than me.
My brother is taller and older than me.
Say this so a young child would understand: The sun is exceedingly hot today.
The sun is very hot today.
Rewrite in the future tense: I visit my cousin and bring some sweets.
I will visit my cousin and bring some sweets.
Rewrite this as if I am speaking: Rahul is hungry, so he opens the fridge.
I am hungry, so I open the fridge.
Make this formal, please: Thanks a lot for helping me out.
Thank you very much for your assistance.
Make it more polite: Open the door for me.
Would you mind opening the door for me?

Shorter, please.

There was a big old tree in the middle of the field, and it was so tall that you could see it from far away.
A very tall old tree stood in the middle of the field and could be seen from far away.
Make this simple for a child: We should attempt to conserve water.
We should try to save water.

Please change this text to the past tense.

I wake up early. I wash my face and eat breakfast. Then I catch the bus.
I woke up early. I washed my face and ate breakfast. Then I caught the bus.

Change "you" to "I".

You must be tired. You worked all day.
I must be tired. I worked all day.
Write this the way friends talk: Please be informed that the class has been cancelled.
The class is cancelled.
Rewrite this politely: Don't touch my things.
Please do not touch my things.
Cut this sentence down: I am writing this message in order to ask whether you can come to the party.
Can you come to the party?
Rewrite in words a child knows: He was extremely delighted with his present.
He was very happy with his present.
Turn this into the present tense: The rain stopped and the sun came out.
The rain stops and the sun comes out.
Make this about we instead of he: He packed his bag and he locked his room.
We packed our bags and we locked our room.
Formal version, please: Sorry I didn't reply sooner.
I apologise for not replying sooner.
Make this polite for a shop: I want two kilos of rice.
May I please have two kilos of rice?
Make this more concise: The teacher asked all of the students to please open up their books to page ten.
The teacher asked the students to open their books to page ten.

Simplify this for a child.

The pupils were instructed to remain silent during the examination.
The students were told to stay quiet during the test.

Make this sentence future tense.

She cleans her room and washes the clothes.
She will clean her room and wash the clothes.
Rewrite in the third person, for a girl named Salma: I love to read, and my favourite place is the roof.
Salma loves to read, and her favourite place is the roof.
Make this less formal: I would be grateful if you could lend me your pen.
Could I borrow your pen?

Rewrite this more politely.

Help me carry this box. It's heavy.
Could you please help me carry this box? It's heavy.

Reduce this to one short sentence.

Our neighbour has a dog. The dog is very friendly. It likes to play with the children.
Our neighbour's friendly dog likes to play with the children.
Use simple words for a young reader: The vehicle halted at the junction.
The car stopped at the corner.
Say this in the past tense: Our teacher gives us a quiz.
Our teacher gave us a quiz.

Change this from "they" to "I".

They forgot their lunch, so they went back for it.
I forgot my lunch, so I went back for it.

Rewrite this letter line more formally.

Hi Mrs Khan, I want to ask about the trip.
Dear Mrs Khan, I would like to ask about the trip.
Make this more courteous: Show me the way to the station.
Could you please show me the way to the station?
Shorten this: It is my belief that we should leave now, because it is getting late.
We should leave now because it is getting late.
Rewrite this for a kid: Please do not consume food in the library.
Please do not eat in the library.

Change the verbs to the present tense.

The farmer opened the gate. He drove the cows to the field. They ate the green grass.
The farmer opens the gate. He drives the cows to the field. They eat the green grass.

Switch this to the first person plural (we):

My sister and I clean the kitchen. I wash the plates and she wipes the table.
My sister and I clean the kitchen. We wash the plates and wipe the table.

Make this casual:

Good afternoon. I wish to enquire whether the shop is open on Sundays.
Hi, is the shop open on Sundays?
Be more polite: Sit down.
Please have a seat.
Say this in fewer words: He did not say anything at all for a very long time.
He said nothing for a long time.

Make this easy for a child to understand.

The woman was unable to locate her spectacles.
The woman could not find her glasses.
Rewrite this in the future tense: Tara writes a letter to her friend.
Tara will write a letter to her friend.

Rewrite so it says "he" instead of "I".

I am learning to swim, and I am a little afraid of deep water.
He is learning to swim, and he is a little afraid of deep water.
Please make this sentence formal: Tell me when the bus comes.
Please inform me when the bus arrives.
Rewrite in a polite way: Stop talking and listen.
Could you please stop talking and listen?

Make this text shorter.

I have been feeling quite tired lately. I think it is because I have not been sleeping well at night. I am going to try to go to bed earlier.
I have felt tired lately, probably from poor sleep. I will try to go to bed earlier.

Rewrite with easy words for a child.

The journey was lengthy, and the travellers were weary when they arrived.
The trip was long, and the travellers were tired when they got there.
Put this in the past tense, please: Hamid fixes his bicycle and rides to the market.
Hamid fixed his bicycle and rode to the market.
Change "she" to "I": She has a cold, so she stays at home.
I have a cold, so I stay at home.

Rewrite this to sound friendly and informal.

We are pleased to invite you to our daughter's birthday party.
Come to our daughter's birthday party!
Make this request polite: Lend me your notebook.
Could I please borrow your notebook?
Trim this sentence: She walked slowly, step by step, along the narrow path that led to the river.
She walked slowly along the narrow path to the river.
Use simpler words: The kitten was terrified of the thunder.
The kitten was very scared of the thunder.
Change to present tense: The soup was hot, so I waited.
The soup is hot, so I wait.

Retell this in the third person about Mr Das.

I teach maths to ten children. I enjoy my work, and I walk home slowly.
Mr Das teaches maths to ten children. He enjoys his work, and he walks home slowly.
Change to formal English: I don't know what time it starts.
I do not know what time it begins.

Make this politer, please.

You are late again. Come on time.
You are late again. Could you please come on time?
Shorten without losing the meaning: In my opinion, I think that the film was very good.
I think the film was very good.
Please simplify this for a child: My grandfather is a very generous man.
My grandfather is a very kind man who likes to give.

Put all of this in the past.

Our neighbours move to a new house. They pack their boxes and say goodbye.
Our neighbours moved to a new house. They packed their boxes and said goodbye.
Make this about "you" instead of "I": I am proud of my garden.
You are proud of your garden.
Make it sound casual: I am extremely grateful for your kind help.
Thanks so much for your help.
Say it more politely: Turn off the light.
Would you please turn off the light?
Write a shorter version of this: There are a lot of books on the shelf, and most of them are very old.
Most of the many books on the shelf are very old.
Rewrite so a young child can read it: The plumber repaired the leaking tap.
The plumber fixed the tap that was dripping.
Make this future tense: The shop opens at nine.
The shop will open at nine.

Change the people from "we" to "they".

We sang a song and we danced in a circle.
They sang a song and they danced in a circle.

Use a more formal tone.

Hey teacher, I forgot my book. Can I get it from my locker?
Hello, teacher. I have forgotten my book. May I fetch it from my locker?
Rewrite politely: Send me the photo.
Could you please send me the photo?

Make this briefer.

On Sunday afternoon we all sat together in the garden. We drank tea and ate biscuits. It was a very nice and relaxing time for everybody.
On Sunday afternoon we sat in the garden, drank tea and ate biscuits. It was relaxing.

Make this simple for a child.

It is essential to wash your hands prior to eating.
You must wash your hands before you eat.
Convert to the present tense: Lucas painted a picture of the sea.
Lucas paints a picture of the sea.
Rewrite in the first person (I): Kiran feels shy, so she stays near her mother.
I feel shy, so I stay near my mother.
Make this easy and casual, like a text to a friend: Kindly let me know whether you will be present.
Tell me if you're coming.
Make this more polite: I need your help.
I would be grateful for your help.
Make this sentence shorter: The reason why I was late is that I missed the bus.
I was late because I missed the bus.
Use words a child would know: The children were exhausted after the competition.
The children were very tired after the game.
Tell it as if it already happened: My sister sings in the choir and I clap.
My sister sang in the choir and I clapped.

Write this about "she" instead of "you".

You found a coin on the road. You gave it to a teacher.
She found a coin on the road. She gave it to a teacher.
Rewrite formally: We're going to need more chairs.
We will require more chairs.

Please make this sound polite.

Move. I can't see the board.
Excuse me, could you please move? I can't see the board.
Shorten: All of the children in the class were extremely excited about the trip.
The children in the class were very excited about the trip.
Simpler words for a young child, please: He ascended the staircase and entered the room.
He went up the stairs and into the room.

Use the future tense for this sentence.

The train leaves from platform two.
The train will leave from platform two.
Change "I" to "they": I think I should leave early, but I will wait for the others.
They think they should leave early, but they will wait for the others.
Rewrite in a casual tone: I am sorry to trouble you, but could you move your bag?
Sorry, could you move your bag?
Rewrite this as a polite question: Tell me your name.
May I please ask your name?
Rewrite shorter: We are going to be able to see the sea from our room.
We can see the sea from our room.

Rewrite this for a child.

The mother comforted her frightened daughter.
The mother calmed her scared daughter.

Change this to present tense.

Priya fell off her bike. She cried for a minute. Then she got up and tried again.
Priya falls off her bike. She cries for a minute. Then she gets up and tries again.

Put this in the first person, as Noah would say it.

Noah brushes his teeth and puts on his coat.
I brush my teeth and put on my coat.
Make this sentence formal: Can you tell me where the office is?
Could you please tell me where the office is?
Make this polite: Give me the bill.
Could I please have the bill?

Cut this text down.

My grandmother lives in a small village. The village is far from the city. She has lived there for her whole life and she loves it.
My grandmother lives in a small village far from the city. She has lived there all her life and loves it.

Make this easy for a child.

The farmer was anxious because the harvest was small this year.
The farmer was worried because he got only a little food from his field this year.
Put it in the past tense: We water the plants every evening.
We watered the plants every evening.
Rewrite for "he" instead of "you": You said that you would call, but you did not.
He said that he would call, but he did not.
Say it in everyday speech: I do not have any objection to that plan.
I'm fine with that plan.
Rewrite more politely: Don't park here.
Please do not park here.
Make this shorter: I do not think that I will be able to come tomorrow.
I don't think I can come tomorrow.
Say this in simple words for a child: Please be careful, the floor is slippery.
Please be careful, the floor is very smooth and you could slip.
Rewrite this so it is in the future tense: The class goes to the park and plays games.
The class will go to the park and play games.

Change "we" to "I".

We waited at the station, and we saw our train come in.
I waited at the station, and I saw my train come in.

Please write this in a formal way.

Hi, I'm Dev. I'm in class nine. I want to join the chess club.
Hello. My name is Dev. I am in class nine. I would like to join the chess club.

Make this sound polite and gentle.

You took my seat. Get up.
Excuse me, I think that is my seat. Could you please move?
Shorter version, please: Please remember to bring your own water bottle with you to the trip.
Please bring your water bottle to the trip.
Rewrite for a young child: The athlete was victorious in the final race.
The runner won the last race.
Change to the present tense, please: Omar helped his mother carry the bags.
Omar helps his mother carry the bags.
Make the narrator "she", and call her Divya: I opened the window and I let the breeze in.
Divya opened the window and she let the breeze in.

Make this casual and short:

Thank you for your message. I will reply as soon as possible.
Thanks for your message. I'll reply soon.
Polite version, please: Let me go first.
Would you mind if I went first?

Use fewer words.

The food at the restaurant was really good, and the people who worked there were really friendly too.
The food at the restaurant was really good and the staff were friendly.

Simplify the words for a child.

We are going to the pharmacy to obtain some medicine.
We are going to the shop to get some medicine.

Make the sentence past tense.

I am tired, so I sleep early.
I was tired, so I slept early.

Switch from "he" to "we".

He is playing football with his friends.
We are playing football with our friends.
Make it formal: Wanna come over after school?
Would you like to come over after school?
Rewrite this to be more polite: Hurry up.
Could you please be quick?
Cut this down: He is the kind of person who always helps others when they need it.
He always helps others in need.

Use easier words so a child can read this.

The moon illuminated the path, and the travellers continued walking.
The moon lit up the path, and the travellers kept walking.

Write this in the future tense.

The baker makes bread. He puts it in the oven and waits.
The baker will make bread. He will put it in the oven and wait.
Say this about me (I), not about Tom: Tom wants to bake a cake, and he needs eggs.
I want to bake a cake, and I need eggs.
Turn this into casual speech: It is imperative that you arrive on time.
Please be on time.
Make this polite: Pick up your toys.
Could you please pick up your toys?
Make this more concise: There is a small garden at the back of our house.
Our house has a small back garden.
Make this simple for a child: Our neighbour is very courteous.
Our neighbour is very polite.
Switch this to the past tense: Zoe forgets her umbrella and gets wet.
Zoe forgot her umbrella and got wet.

Rewrite in the third person (she):

I sit by the window and watch the rain. My tea is cold, but I do not mind.
She sits by the window and watches the rain. Her tea is cold, but she does not mind.
Rewrite for a formal notice board: Don't leave your bikes in front of the gate.
Please do not leave bicycles in front of the gate.

Make this more respectful.

Tell the teacher I need a pencil.
Please tell the teacher that I need a pencil.

Shorten this note.

Dear Anita, I just wanted to write to you to say thank you very much for the lovely present that you gave me for my birthday.
Dear Anita, thank you very much for the lovely birthday present.
Rewrite in easy words: The baker prepared a delicious loaf of bread.
The baker made a tasty loaf of bread.
Rewrite in the present tense: My brother broke a cup and said sorry.
My brother breaks a cup and says sorry.

Change "they" to "you".

They have finished their homework, and they can go out.
You have finished your homework, and you can go out.

Make this relaxed, the way I would say it to my cousin.

I am delighted to hear that you passed your exam.
I'm so happy you passed your exam!
Rewrite politely: Answer my question.
Could you please answer my question?
Say it in fewer words: Each and every one of us has to wash our hands before eating.
Everyone has to wash their hands before eating.

Simplify this for a young child.

The puppy was extremely energetic and would not remain still.
The puppy had lots of energy and would not stay still.

The verbs should be in the future tense here.

They are building a small bridge over the stream.
They will be building a small bridge over the stream.
Rewrite this from "I" to "we": I painted the wall and I cleaned the floor.
We painted the wall and we cleaned the floor.

Make this formal.

Sorry, I can't make it to the party.
I apologise, but I am unable to attend the party.
Be more polite in this sentence: Go away, I'm busy.
I'm sorry, but I'm busy right now.
Shorten this sentence: The bus, which was very crowded, arrived late at the stop.
The crowded bus arrived late.

Say this simply for a child.

The tailor altered the dress so that it would fit her properly.
The tailor changed the dress so that it would fit her well.
Make it past tense: The cat sleeps on the sofa and purrs.
The cat slept on the sofa and purred.
Tell this about a boy named Idris, in the third person: I saved some money, and I bought a football.
Idris saved some money, and he bought a football.
Write this in plain, casual English: The train has been delayed by twenty minutes.
The train is twenty minutes late.
Make this request more polite: Bring me a cup of tea.
Could you please bring me a cup of tea?
Make this brief: I went to the library and I borrowed two books from the library.
I borrowed two books from the library.
Use simple words for a child: She was reluctant to speak in front of the class.
She did not want to talk in front of the class.

Please put this in the present tense.

We sat in the garden. Mum poured the tea and Dad read the newspaper.
We sit in the garden. Mum pours the tea and Dad reads the newspaper.

Change the speaker from "I" to "he".

I am the youngest in my family. My brothers help me, and I thank them.
He is the youngest in his family. His brothers help him, and he thanks them.
Please change this to a formal request: Give me a day off on Friday.
I would like to request a day off on Friday.

Say this in a polite way.

I want to ask something. Listen to me.
May I ask something? Could you please listen to me?

Make this shorter.

Our teacher is very kind. She is also very patient. She never shouts at us, even when we make mistakes.
Our teacher is kind and patient and never shouts, even at our mistakes.
Rewrite this in easy words for a child: The mountain was covered with snow, and the temperature was extremely low.
The mountain was covered with snow, and it was very cold.
Turn this into the future tense: I call you after dinner.
I will call you after dinner.
Rewrite with "they" in place of "she": She is waiting at the gate for her friends.
They are waiting at the gate for their friends.

Make this sound casual.

I would prefer to eat at home this evening.
I'd rather eat at home tonight.
Make it polite: Switch off your phone.
Would you please switch off your phone?
Shorten this a bit: It was a very cold and windy day in the month of January.
It was a cold, windy January day.

Make this simpler for a young child.

The librarian requested that we return the books.
The librarian asked us to give back the books.
Make this past tense: Nadia chooses a red kite and runs to the field.
Nadia chose a red kite and ran to the field.
Make this first person singular: The boy said that he was late and that his bag was heavy.
I said that I was late and that my bag was heavy.

Rewrite in formal language.

Hi, it's Ali. I can't find my bag. Has anyone seen it?
Hello, this is Ali. I am unable to find my bag. Has anyone seen it?
Make this sound more polite: Share your lunch with me.
Would you please share your lunch with me?
Cut it down to fewer words: It is not possible for me to carry all of these bags by myself.
I can't carry all these bags by myself.

Easy words for a child, please.

The boy was bewildered because he could not understand the instructions.
The boy was confused because he could not understand what to do.
Change the tense to the present: The film began and everyone went quiet.
The film begins and everyone goes quiet.

Change "you" to "we":

You can sit here. You will see the whole stage.
We can sit here. We will see the whole stage.
Make this chatty: I am pleased to announce that our team has won.
Great news, our team won!
Rewrite politely: Say it again.
Could you please say that again?

Please make this text shorter.

The festival is on Friday. There will be music and dancing. Everyone in the village is going to be there, and all are welcome.
The festival is on Friday, with music and dancing. Everyone in the village is welcome.
Simplify this sentence for a child: The fruit seller sells a variety of fresh produce.
The fruit seller sells many kinds of fresh fruit and vegetables.

Write this sentence in the future tense.

Our team wins the match.
Our team will win the match.
Rewrite about a girl named Lina (third person): I never go out without my umbrella, and I keep a small one in my bag.
Lina never goes out without her umbrella, and she keeps a small one in her bag.
Formal, please: Don't worry, I'll fix it.
Please do not worry. I will repair it.

Make this politer.

Give me a seat. I'm tired.
May I please have a seat? I'm tired.
Tighten this sentence: The movie that we watched last night was a movie about animals.
The movie we watched last night was about animals.
Rewrite in words a young child can follow: Kindly assemble near the entrance.
Please come together near the door.

Past tense, please.

The clock strikes six. Mum comes home and we eat together.
The clock struck six. Mum came home and we ate together.

Switch "I" to "you".

I am sure I closed the door, and I locked it.
You are sure you closed the door, and you locked it.
Change this to casual English: Please accept my apologies for the delay.
Sorry about the delay.
Make this polite for a neighbour: Take your dog away.
Could you please take your dog away?
Make this shorter: He has a habit of waking up very early in the morning every day.
He wakes up very early every day.

Write this in simple words a child knows.

It was an exceedingly peaceful evening.
It was a very quiet evening.
Change to the present tense: He wore his blue shirt and combed his hair.
He wears his blue shirt and combs his hair.

Retell in the first person (we).

The twins share a room. They tidy it on Sundays, and they never fight about it.
We share a room. We tidy it on Sundays, and we never fight about it.

Make this more formal for an email to a teacher.

Hi miss, I didn't do the homework. Can I give it tomorrow?
Dear Miss, I have not completed the homework. May I submit it tomorrow?
Rewrite this politely: Don't make noise.
Please do not make noise.

Shorten the message.

Hi Raju, I hope you are doing well. I am just checking whether you have got the book that I lent to you last week.
Hi Raju, have you still got the book I lent you last week?

Make this easy to read for a child.

The merchant purchased several metres of cloth and departed.
The shopkeeper bought a few metres of cloth and left.
Make this future tense: Mina plants a mango tree near the wall.
Mina will plant a mango tree near the wall.
Rewrite it with "he" instead of "she": She asked her uncle for a ride.
He asked his uncle for a ride.

Say this in a casual way:

I have not yet had the opportunity to read your letter.
I haven't read your letter yet.
Polite, please: Come here.
Would you please come here?
Reduce the number of words: At the present time, the shop is closed for lunch.
The shop is closed for lunch.
Simplify for a child: He is an excellent cook.
He is a very good cook.

The students sat quietly and listened.

Amara takes the early train, and she reads on the way.

Clean the board. Do it now.

I lost my pencil, so I borrowed one.
I lose my pencil, so I borrow one.

We would like to thank you for attending.

The river was too wide and deep to cross without a boat. The villagers had one old boat, the ferryman's.

Rewrite this so that a child can understand it.

My cousin resides in a large city.
My cousin lives in a big city.

Put this text in the future tense.

Grandpa takes his walk. He greets the neighbours and buys milk.
Grandpa will take his walk. He will greet the neighbours and buy milk.

Maya hurt her knee. She sat down and rubbed it, and then she walked on.
I hurt my knee. I sat down and rubbed it, and then I walked on.

The doctor advised him to rest, and he obeyed.

Leo drew a map and showed it to us.

Leave me alone. I want to study.

We take a rickshaw and reach the temple.

Wake up the baby. It's time for milk.

Hana packed her bag and waited at the door.

I keep a diary, and I write in it every night.
